meta.title: Harness — Agent Harness Course
meta.description: Build the harness. Let the model drive. A 17-lesson interactive Agent Harness course.

home.hero_subtitle_initial: Build the Harness. Let the Model Drive.
home.core_pattern_desc: Every AI coding agent shares the same loop: call the model, execute tools, feed results back. The Harness adds policy, permissions, memory, coordination, and lifecycle control around it.
home.message_flow_desc: Watch the messages array grow as the agent loop executes
home.learning_path_desc_initial: 17 progressive lessons, from a simple loop to deterministic orchestration and goal closure
home.layers_desc: Five concerns that compose into a complete Agent Harness
home.hero_subtitle: Start with one Agent Loop, then add tools, memory, tasks, teams, workflows, and a goal-completion gate.
home.panel_definition: The model makes decisions. The Harness supplies an environment where those decisions can become observable, constrained actions.
home.harness_tools_desc: Callable capabilities such as files, Shell, browsers, and APIs.
home.harness_knowledge_desc: Domain instructions and references loaded when the task needs them.
home.harness_observation_desc: Results, logs, diffs, and state that let the model see what happened.
home.harness_action_desc: Stable boundaries that turn model intent into operations in the world.
home.harness_permissions_desc: Approval, sandboxing, and trust rules that decide what may run.
home.philosophy_title_2: The Harness gives it a world to act in.
home.philosophy_desc: The model reasons and chooses. The Harness exposes context, executes requests, reports outcomes, and enforces boundaries.
home.value_intro: Harness engineering is not a substitute for model intelligence. It is the work of making that intelligence effective, observable, and safe in a real domain.
home.value_tools_desc: Give the model precise, composable ways to change its environment.
home.value_context_desc: Keep the right instructions and observations available during long work.
home.value_state_desc: Let plans, tasks, and memory survive beyond one model response.
home.value_control_desc: Use permissions and completion criteria to establish clear boundaries.
home.learning_path_desc: Read in order to see the system grow, or enter any lesson directly to inspect one mechanism.
home.stages_title: Six stages from action to closure.
home.core_loop_title: Watch the loop do real work.
home.core_loop_desc: A request becomes a model decision, a Bash call, an observed result, and a final answer. The loop stays small; the Harness around it grows.
home.closing_line_1: One loop is enough to begin.
home.closing_line_2: 17 lessons are enough to build the Harness.
home.loop_path_label: User to model to tool use to tool result to model

course.title: Build an Agent Harness, one mechanism at a time.
course.subtitle: Follow s01 through s17 to move from a minimal model/tool loop to integrated, resumable, goal-directed execution.
course.boundary_title: The reading order is linear. The source lineage is not always linear.
course.boundary_desc: Lessons s11–s14 isolate different mechanisms, s15 integrates the runtime, and s16–s17 focus on orchestration and goal completion. You can open any lesson without completing prerequisites.
course.open_access: All 17 lessons are open · start anywhere · no prerequisite lock
course.stage_foundations_desc: Build the loop, expand its tool surface, then establish permission and lifecycle boundaries.
course.stage_planning_context_desc: Keep long work directed, isolate subtasks, load knowledge on demand, and recover context space.
course.stage_memory_tasks_desc: Preserve reusable knowledge and turn goals into durable dependency graphs.
course.stage_concurrency_scheduling_desc: Move slow work off the main loop and create work at the right time.
course.stage_agents_capabilities_desc: Coordinate persistent teammates and connect external MCP tools.
course.stage_integration_closure_desc: Combine the Harness, make fixed workflows resumable, and let evidence decide when the goal is complete.

topics.title: Topics
topics.subtitle: Explore the 17 lessons by mechanism instead of reading order
topics.tools: How the model acts: the loop, tool dispatch, permission boundaries, and lifecycle hooks.
topics.planning: How work stays directed: plans, isolated subagents, on-demand knowledge, and goal evaluation.
topics.memory: How useful context survives limits and important knowledge persists across sessions.
topics.concurrency: How slow, scheduled, and fixed-shape work runs without blocking the core loop.
topics.collaboration: How tasks, teammates, external tools, and the integrated runtime form a platform.

compare.title: Compare any two lessons.
compare.subtitle: Inspect the actual source, symbols, tools, and architecture of A and B. Reading order does not imply complete source inheritance.
compare.boundary_default: The values below are calculated directly from the selected source files. Added and removed mean present on one side only; they do not assert a parent-child relationship.
compare.boundary_s10_s13: s10 teaches a single-Agent persistent task graph. s13 is a team runtime that uses task ownership, mailboxes, atomic claims, and task-bound worktrees; it is not a cumulative copy of s10.
compare.boundary_s14_s15: s14 isolates MCP discovery and invocation. s15 integrates MCP with memory, tasks, teams, scheduling, permissions, and one Agent Loop.
compare.boundary_s15_s16: s15 remains model-driven around one integrated loop. s16 gives fixed orchestration to a Workflow script with parallel stages, a journal, and resume semantics.
compare.boundary_s16_s17: s16 decides when a scripted workflow run has completed. s17 separately asks whether the user's durable goal has enough evidence to stop the Agent Loop.

session_questions.s01: How can a model keep calling tools until the task is done?
session_questions.s02: How can capabilities expand without changing the core loop?
session_questions.s03: How should the Harness decide whether an operation may run?
session_questions.s04: How can behavior extend without invading the loop?
session_questions.s05: How can long work stay visible and on course?
session_questions.s06: How can a subtask get clean context without losing the main thread?
session_questions.s07: How can specialist knowledge load only when needed?
session_questions.s08: How can work continue when the context window fills up?
session_questions.s09: Which knowledge should survive across sessions?
session_questions.s10: How can goals become persistent, ordered work?
session_questions.s11: How can slow commands run without blocking reasoning?
session_questions.s12: How can the Harness create work on a schedule?
session_questions.s13: How can multiple agents coordinate reliably?
session_questions.s14: How can external tools enter the same tool pool?
session_questions.s15: How do many mechanisms fit around one loop?
session_questions.s16: How can fixed workflows run in parallel and resume safely?
session_questions.s17: Who decides whether the whole goal is truly complete?

session_insights.s01: The smallest useful agent is a loop that calls the model, runs tools, and feeds results back.
session_insights.s02: The loop stays stable while capabilities register into a dispatch table.
session_insights.s03: Dangerous actions need a harness decision point before the shell runs.
session_insights.s04: Cross-cutting behavior belongs around the loop, not tangled inside it.
session_insights.s05: Explicit plans keep long-running work visible and correctable.
session_insights.s06: Subagents give each subtask a clean message history while preserving the main thread.
session_insights.s07: Inject specialized knowledge only when the task actually needs it.
session_insights.s08: Compression keeps the conversation usable when the context window gets crowded.
session_insights.s09: Some facts should survive summarization and future sessions.
session_insights.s10: A task graph turns vague goals into ordered, observable work.
session_insights.s11: The agent can keep reasoning while slow work completes elsewhere.
session_insights.s12: Recurring work should be created by the harness, not remembered by the model.
session_insights.s13: Persistent teammates work reliably when the runtime owns messaging, atomic claims, and task-bound directories.
session_insights.s14: External services become agent tools through a standard discovery and call protocol.
session_insights.s15: The integrated harness is still one loop, surrounded by the systems introduced across the course.
session_insights.s16: When orchestration has a fixed shape, code can make it parallel, deterministic, and resumable.
session_insights.s17: A durable goal keeps the loop working until an independent evaluator finds completion evidence.
